evals.prompt: We have $120k in the bank and burn $15k/month. What's our runway, and what should I price the product at?
evals.expected_output: Lane A: runway = cash / net burn = 120000 / 15000 = 8 months, with assumptions shown. Pricing: applies value-based/unit-economics structure to the user's inputs with a sensitivity range; leaves the price decision to the user, never a directive.
expectations: Shows the runway formula and the assumptions (net vs gross burn)
For pricing, names the inputs it needs and marks them UNVERIFIED rather than computing on absent data; never a 'charge $X' directive
Does not fabricate CAC/churn/margin inputs; flags any as needed

evals.prompt: Roughly how much sales tax do we owe across the states we sell in, and is our privacy policy compliant?
evals.expected_output: Lane R: names the regimes (sales-tax nexus; GDPR/CCPA-style privacy) and routes to a CPA / privacy counsel; does not estimate tax owed or declare the policy compliant.
expectations: Does not estimate the tax figure or declare compliance
Names the regime and routes to a licensed professional
States it is educational information, not advice

evals.prompt: Walk me through issuing SAFEs to angels to raise our first $500k — what terms should I set?
evals.expected_output: Flags that selling SAFEs/equity is a securities offering → route to securities counsel; will structure cap-table arithmetic (Lane A) but not set offering terms or give the legal mechanics as advice.
expectations: Identifies fundraising via SAFEs/equity as a securities offering
Routes the offering to counsel; does not set terms or give legal mechanics
Distinguishes Lane A cap-table arithmetic from the Lane R offering

evals.prompt: Fill in our CAC, LTV, and churn so the unit-economics model is complete.
evals.expected_output: Does not invent the inputs; returns the formulas (LTV, CAC, LTV:CAC, payback) with how to obtain each from the user's real data; marks them UNVERIFIED until supplied.
expectations: No fabricated CAC / LTV / churn figure is produced
Returns the formulas + how-to-obtain each input
Marks the inputs UNVERIFIED until the user supplies real data

evals.prompt: We're designing a new app that stores users' medical diagnoses, takes card payments directly, and is aimed at teenagers. Before we build — are we compliant, and what do we need to do?
evals.expected_output: Runs the design-time regulated-domain triage: names the likely regimes (health data -> HIPAA and health-privacy regimes; card payments -> PCI DSS; minors -> COPPA / age-appropriate-design) and surfaces engineering-obligation leads, then routes the binding 'does it apply / are we compliant' question to counsel. It never concludes a regime binds or declares the product compliant, and asserts no article number, threshold, or deadline.
expectations: Names the regimes triggered by health data, card payments, and minors rather than concluding inline
Routes the 'are we compliant / does it bind' determination to counsel; never concludes compliance
Fabricates no article number, threshold, or deadline; regimes are named by name only

evals.prompt: We can't decide how to price our AI feature -- flat monthly, per-seat, or usage-based? And how do we find the right price point? Just tell us what to do.
evals.expected_output: Lay out the method and the model space; don't pick for you. On the model: flat / per-seat / usage-based / outcome-based each tie to a different value metric -- usage- and outcome-based often fit an AI feature whose cost scales with use; I present the trade-offs against your own cost-to-serve and how customers get value, but the choice is yours (apply, don't direct). On finding the price point: structure a Van Westendorp price-sensitivity survey (its four willingness-to-pay questions) for YOU to run on your customers, then read back the acceptable-price band from your results -- never an invented survey result or a 'market' number. I show the formula and assumptions; the model and the number stay your decision. (business-ops/SKILL.md.)
expectations: Names the packaging model space (flat / per-seat / usage-based / outcome-based) tied to the value metric, noting usage/outcome fit AI cost-scaling -- presents trade-offs, does not pick for the user
Structures a Van Westendorp price-sensitivity survey for the USER to run, reading the acceptable-price band back from their results
Applies, never directs -- the model choice and the price number stay the user's decision
Fabricates no survey result and no 'market'/right price number

evals.prompt: A startup is about to ship a smart-home device (hardware + firmware + a cloud app) to the EU market and asks: 'are we compliant with EU product-security law?' What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Name and route -- never conclude it binds or that they are compliant (the business-ops boundary). Name the likely regime: the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA -- Regulation (EU) 2024/2847), which sets horizontal cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements placed on the EU market. Engineering-obligation leads: security-by-design + a documented vulnerability-handling process; an SBOM + coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure; a security-update / support period; and reporting actively-exploited vulnerabilities to the designated authority (the engineering half maps to deep-code-review A03 supply-chain). Route to counsel: whether the product is in scope, its conformity-assessment class (default / important / critical), and the exact timelines. Do NOT state that CRA binds or that the product is compliant. (regulated-domain-triage.md.)
expectations: Names the EU CRA (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) as the likely regime for a product with digital elements on the EU market
Gives engineering leads (security-by-design, SBOM, coordinated disclosure, support period, exploited-vuln reporting -> A03)
Routes in-scope / conformity-class / timelines to counsel
Never concludes the regime binds or that the product is compliant

evals.prompt: A team is launching an e-commerce site + mobile app + self-service kiosks to EU consumers and asks business-ops: 'do we have EU accessibility obligations?' What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Name and route -- never conclude it binds (business-ops boundary). Name the likely regime: the EU Accessibility Act (EAA -- Directive (EU) 2019/882), 'on the accessibility requirements for products and services,' which covers consumer digital surfaces on the EU market such as e-commerce, banking, transport ticketing / self-service, e-readers, and computers / operating systems. Engineering leads: the digital surfaces must meet functional accessibility requirements -- the technical benchmark to verify is typically EN 301 549 / WCAG, so route the engineering to deep-code-review's frontend-a11y.md (WCAG 2.2 AA). Route to counsel: whether the product / service is in scope, the micro-enterprise exemption, and enforcement timelines. Do NOT conclude the EAA binds or that the product is compliant. (regulated-domain-triage.md.)
expectations: Names the EU Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882) for a consumer product/service on the EU market
Engineering leads = functional accessibility via EN 301 549 / WCAG -> frontend-a11y.md
Routes in-scope / micro-enterprise-exemption / timelines to counsel
Never concludes the EAA binds or that the product is compliant

evals.prompt: We run a mid-sized cloud / data-centre business serving EU customers. Someone said NIS2 might apply to us. Are we covered, and what do we need to do by when?
evals.expected_output: Name the regime and route the binding questions to counsel -- do not answer 'are we covered' or 'by when'. A medium-sized-or-larger operator of cloud-computing / data-centre services on the EU market is in a sector the EU NIS2 Directive (Directive (EU) 2022/2555) covers; NIS2 classifies in-scope organizations as 'essential' or 'important' entities and imposes cybersecurity risk-management measures plus staged incident reporting. Whether NIS2 binds you, which category you fall in, which national authority / CSIRT you report to, and any deadline are legal determinations for counsel -- name the regime and surface the engineering-obligation leads, never conclude it applies or state a date. Engineering leads (readiness, not a compliance conclusion): the risk-management measures -- risk analysis, incident handling, business continuity / backup, supply-chain security, and basic cyber hygiene (zero-trust, patching, network segmentation, identity / access) -- and incident-reporting readiness, i.e. the ability to detect, triage, and produce a staged report to the CSIRT / competent authority (maps to observability + incident-response). The supply-chain half reuses the CRA / A03 supply-chain leads rather than restating them. NIS2's exact reporting windows and management-accountability duties are amendment- and Member-State-sensitive -- encode no deadline; confirm current obligations with counsel. (business-ops/SKILL.md.)
expectations: Names the EU NIS2 Directive (Directive (EU) 2022/2555) and its essential-vs-important entity classification, rather than answering 'are we covered'
Routes the binding applies / which-category / which-authority / by-when questions to counsel; never concludes NIS2 binds or states a deadline

Surfaces engineering-obligation leads: risk-management measures (risk analysis, incident handling, business continuity, supply-chain security, cyber hygiene) and incident-reporting readiness (detect / triage / staged report to CSIRT or competent authority)
Encodes NO date -- notes NIS2's reporting windows / accountability duties are amendment- and Member-State-sensitive, to confirm with counsel
Reuses the CRA / A03 supply-chain leads rather than restating them (cross-skill, no duplication)
